data.narrative:
Dexterity is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon and co-founders, currently valued at $1.65B on $291M raised. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private robotics peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). Primary peers include Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C).

Two methods were applied. Peer-Median anchors to the median valuation of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, yielding $1.6B and establishing a $1.0B–$1.8B range. Stage-Progression applies a typical Series B-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.9x to the $1.6B last post-money valuation, implying $3.1B. This methodological spread reflects uncertainty around whether Dexterity's profile aligns more closely with current peer trading ranges or justifies growth-stage multiples.

Triangulating these two methods produces a median valuation of $2.4B, with a low of $1.4B and high of $3.6B. The wide range underscores key uncertainties: the magnitude of step-up pricing in Series B-to-C financing within robotics, and whether Dexterity's proprietary capabilities command a premium relative to the observed peer set. The current $1.65B valuation sits near the peer median, leaving upside contingent on demonstrable differentiation and capital-intensity runway.
